note: AN ANCHOR WHERE IT CAN NEVER MATCH, and the one case in this group that ALREADY AGREES -- (nil nil) on both sides -- which is why it carries `expect: agree' inside a divergent row. It agrees for two different reasons, and that is the point: Emacs matches nothing because `\\`' can only match at offset 0 and there is an `a' before it, while kg matches nothing because it reads `\\`' as a literal backtick and the subject has none (phase26-anchor-literal-backtick-today measures that directly). After 26.2 teaches the spellings the answer must still be (nil nil) -- an implementation that made a mid-pattern anchor match anything would fail here.
